In ''The Star Wars Holiday Special'', Lumpy was portrayed by three-feet-eleven-inches-tall actress [[Patty Maloney]].<ref name="Maloney interview 2">{{WebCite|url=http://www.starwarsholidayspecial.com/text/patty_maloney.htm|text=Interview with Patty Maloney, "Lumpy" By SKot Kirkwood - November 8, 2008|work=The Star Wars Holiday Special|archivedate=20181016165010}}</ref> As both Lumpy and several of the characters he interacts with in the show speak Shyriiwook, Maloney attended a class that educated her on the language so that she could better respond to cues during filming.<ref name="Lumpy speaks" /> Lumpy's voice, provided by a baby [[Wikipedia:American Black Bear|black bear]] named [[Tarik]], was added during [[Wikipedia:Post-production|post-production]] by [[Wikipedia:Sound design|sound designer]] [[Ben Burtt]],<ref name="Bad Feeling" /> a situation that forced Maloney to convey Lumpy's emotions through the use of [[Wikipedia:Mime artist|mime]] during shooting.<ref name="Lumpy speaks" /> Burtt recorded Tarik's voice at the [[Wikipedia:San Jose, California|San Jose]] Baby Zoo in [[Wikipedia:California|California]]. He was searching for a bear with a cute growl and settled on Tarik after discovering that [[Pooh]], the bear who had provided Chewbacca's voice for ''Star Wars'', had grown from a toddler into a snarling adult.<ref name="Travel Guide">[[Galactic Phrase Book & Travel Guide (real-life book)|''Galactic Phrase Book and Travel Guide'']]</ref>

[[File:PattyMaloney.jpg|thumb|right|200px|Patty Maloney played Lumpy in ''The Star Wars Holiday Special''.]]
Lumpy's costume was created by makeup artist [[Stan Winston]] and two of his friends. The three constructed all three new Wookiee suits out of human hair,<ref name="Bad Feeling" /> which resulted in the costumes being very hot for the actors to wear<ref name="Maloney interview 2" />&mdash;Binder has speculated that Maloney lost ten pounds during filming.<ref name="Binder official interview" /> After Lumpy's costume was completed, it was tailored to Maloney's figure.<ref name="Maloney interview 2" /> Winston also developed Lumpy's mask, which made use of cutting-edge [[Wikipedia:Animatronics|animatronics]] technology that he himself created. Wires ran from the mask down the arms of the costume, and Maloney pulled on rings at the ends of the wires to move Lumpy's nose and mouth. When Maloney was required to pick up props during closeup shots, Winston sat behind her and worked the strings. Although the area around them was painted black, Maloney's own eyes were visible through the mask; she used them to convey as much expression as she could.<ref name="Lumpy speaks" />

The tightness of the mask around Maloney's eyes prevented her from breathing anywhere save through her mouth, however; crew members were at hand to stick a straw through her mouth and provide her with oxygen after shooting scenes that required her to run.<ref name="Maloney interview 2" /> Chewbacca actor [[Peter Mayhew]] has suggested that the new masks created for Lumpy, Malla, and Itchy were "too much," with too many cables running around and someone trying to operate them. Even so, he credits the interaction of four Wookiees of different ages and sizes as inspiring the Ewoks in [[1983]]'s [[Star Wars: Episode VI Return of the Jedi|''Return of the Jedi'']], especially the performance of the Ewok-sized Lumpy.<ref name="Peter Mayhew Interview Insider 28">{{InsiderCite|28|Chewie: An Exclusive Interview with Peter Mayhew}}</ref> Lumpy's mask and feet are currently housed in the Lucasfilm archives,<ref name="Bad Feeling" /><ref name="Survival">{{SWArchive|url=movies/saga/20081120a.html|text=Holiday Special: What Has Survived?}}</ref> and special effects artist [[Don Bies]] has stated that the costume's entire bodysuit is as well.<ref name="Bad Feeling" />

Lumpy's scenes were filmed over approximately ten days. [[Harrison Ford]], who played Han Solo, had to shoot a scene with Maloney several times due to his habit of forgetting that the character she played was male. Maloney remembers her time as Lumpy very fondly, and she has described the character as an impish and rebellious boy who is very active and curious.<ref name="Lumpy speaks" /> She has appeared at at least one autograph signing and she occasionally receives fan mail from a large ''[[Star Wars]]'' fanbase that is very interested in the character of Lumpy.<ref name="Maloney interview 2" />

===Character development===
{{Quote|When I set out to recast and redeem the Lumpy story in THE BLACK FLEET CRISIS, I was drawing on a copy of the Star Wars Storybook which Lucasfilm loaned to me after turning down my proposal to give Chewbacca a polygamous family&mdash;I was obliged to work with the family Chewbacca already had.|Michael P. Kube-McDowell|<ref name="Recast Redeem">{{WebCite|url=http://www.lucasfan.com/swtv/index3.html|text=Star Wars Holiday Special Opinions|work=[https://web.archive.org/web/19981212015351/http://lucasfan.com LucasFan.com]|archivedate=20200120144211|nolive=1}}</ref>}}
''The Star Wars Holiday Special'' aired once on television and was almost universally panned.<ref name="Comedy Hour" /><ref name="farce1">{{WebCite|url=https://www.latimes.com/archives/la-xpm-2008-nov-16-ca-starwars16-story.html|text=May the farce be with you (page 1 of 3)|work=Los Angeles Times|archivedate=20191115073321}}</ref><ref name="multimedia">{{WebCite|url=http://starwarsholidayspecial.com/multimedia.htm|text=Multimedia|work=The Star Wars Holiday Special|archivedate=20180827065634}}</ref><ref name="panned">{{SW|url=video/bucket-head|series=Making Episode II Webdocs|text=Part 9: Bucket Head}}</ref><ref name="Jawa">{{InsiderCite|94|Jawa's Corner}}</ref> Much of the criticism stemmed from the opening fifteen minutes of the special, which exclusively features Lumpy and his family speaking to each other in untranslated Shyriiwook.<ref name="Binder official interview" /><ref name="Comedy Hour 3">{{WebCite|url=http://www.vanityfair.com/magazine/2008/12/star_wars_special200812?currentPage=3|text=The Han Solo Comedy Hour! (page 3 of 3)|work=Vanity Fair|archivedate=20081225130516}}</ref><ref name="Top 20">{{InsiderCite|83|20 Most Memorable Moments of the Expanded Universe}}</ref><ref name="farce2">{{WebCite|url=http://articles.latimes.com/2008/nov/16/entertainment/ca-starwars16/2|text=May the farce be with you (page 2 of 3)|author=Donald Liebenson|date=2008-11-16|work=Los Angeles Times|archivedate=20160911152459}}</ref><ref name="ABC News">{{WebCite|url=http://abcnews.go.com/Nightline/story?id=4034365&page=2|text=Holiday Specials Gone Bad|author=John Berman and Ted Gernstein|date=2007-12-20|archivedate=20180802193011}}</ref> George Lucas himself has expressed regret that it was ever produced.<ref name="Comedy Hour" /> Lumpy has garnered mockery specific to his character&mdash;''Star Wars'' author [[Jon Bradley Snyder]] has called him "[[Wikipedia:Adam Rich|Adam Rich]] with fur, a long-haired gangly precursor to the Ewoks,"<ref name="Holiday Special article">{{InsiderCite|23|The Star Wars Holiday Special (article)|''The Star Wars Holiday Special''}}</ref> and [[Wikipedia:Total Film|''Total Film'']] magazine ranked him fourth on their [[2010]] list of "30 stupidest [sic] Star Wars characters."<ref name="stupid">{{WebCite|url=http://www.totalfilm.com/features/30-stupidest-star-wars-characters/lumpy|text=30 Stupidest Star Wars Characters - The Farce is strong with them|author=Simon Kinnear|date=2010-11-02|work=Total Film - The Modern Guide to Movies|archivedate=20101104235939}}</ref> Nevertheless, Lumpy has since appeared in a number of works of the ''Star Wars'' [[Star Wars Legends|Expanded Universe]]. [[1979|One year]] after the ''Holiday Special'' aired, a companion children's book called ''[[The Wookiee Storybook]]'' was released. It centers around a misadventure of Lumpy's and was being written by [[Eleanor Ehrhardt]] during the ''Holiday Special''{{'s}} production. [[Wikipedia:Illustrator|Illustrator]] [[Patricia Wynne]] was unaware of what the Wookiee costumes from the ''Holiday Special'' looked like and was forced to visually construct the characters from scratch. Her sketches were sent directly to Lucas, who allowed her a large amount of creative freedom under a tight deadline.<ref name="Monster Ships" /> ''The Wookiee Storybook'' introduced several new elements of Wookiee culture and was the first work to establish Lumpy's full name as "Lumpawarrump"<ref name="The Wookiee Storybook" /> rather than the earlier-asserted "Lumwarrump."<ref name="Bad Feeling" />

[[File:Animatronics.jpg|thumb|left|250px|Lumpy's mask and animatronic cables, as stored in the Lucasfilm archives]]
Lumpawarrump's next appearance was a small role in the [[Star Wars (1977) 91|ninety-first issue]] of [[Marvel Comics]]' ongoing [[Star Wars (1977)|''Star Wars'' series]].<ref name="Wookiee World" /> The Expanded Universe experienced a renaissance in [[1991]],<ref name="Novel Approach">{{InsiderCite|66|Novel Approach}}</ref> and early stories such as the ''Holiday Special'' and ''The Wookiee Storybook'' were only gradually accepted into [[canon]].<ref name="EGTC" /><ref name="Jawa" /> Lumpawarrump was mentioned in only a few sources throughout the 1990s.<ref name="EGTC" /><ref name="Chronicles">''[[Star Wars Chronicles]]''</ref> When [[Wikipedia:Author|author]] [[Michael P. Kube-McDowell]] was contracted to write ''[[The Black Fleet Crisis]]'' Trilogy of novels in [[1996]], he drafted a story outline that involved Chewbacca returning to Kashyyyk sixteen years after the events of the original ''Star Wars'' film in order to find a mate. He was subsequently told by Lucasfilm Ltd. that Chewbacca already had a family,<ref name="Monster Ships" /> and he accordingly revamped the plot to feature Chewbacca returning home to attend a coming-of-age ceremony for Lumpawarrump.<ref name="Tyrant's Test" /> McDowell has referred to the writing process as an effort to clean up the canon around Lumpawarrump,<ref name="Monster Ships" /> and he was pleased that he was able to "recast and redeem" Lumpawarrump's story.<ref name="Recast Redeem" /> McDowell renamed the character "Lumpawaroo," or "Waroo" for short, in the trilogy's [[Tyrant's Test|final chapter]], a name that Lumpawarrump earns after completing his coming-of-age ceremony.<ref name="Tyrant's Test" />

Lumpawaroo's birth was depicted in [[A. C. Crispin]]'s [[1998]] novel ''[[Rebel Dawn]]'' at a point in time three years before the events of ''The Star Wars Holiday Special'',<ref name="Rebel Dawn" /> contrary to the ''Holiday Special''{{'s}} script's assertion that the character was ten years old.<ref name="Bad Feeling" /> Lumpawaroo then made two brief appearances in [[Star Wars: The New Jedi Order|''The New Jedi Order'']] book series after the death of his father,<ref name="Hero's Trial" /><ref name="The Unifying Force" /> and a young Lumpawarrump played a large role in the [[2003]] [[eBook]] novella ''[[A Forest Apart]]'', written by [[Troy Denning]].<ref name="A Forest Apart" /> Although Denning found it difficult to write a story starring almost exclusively Wookiees, he enjoyed the experience.<ref name="Ghost Stories">{{SWArchive|url=eu/lit/novel/f20030303/index.html|text=Troy Denning: ''Ghost'' Stories}}</ref> Lumpawaroo's most recent appearances have been in the novels ''[[Legacy of the Force: Inferno]]'' and ''[[Legacy of the Force: Fury]]'', two volumes of the ''[[Star Wars: Legacy of the Force]]'' book series published in [[2007]].<ref name="Fury" /><ref name="Inferno" />

Several discrepancies regarding Lumpawaroo exist within ''Star Wars'' canon. The [[1997]] trivia book ''[[Diplomatic Corps Entrance Exam]]'' misspells Lumpawarrump as Lumpawarump,<ref name="Diplomatic Corps">''[[Diplomatic Corps Entrance Exam]]''</ref> and in ''[[Before the Storm]]'', the first chapter of ''The Black Fleet Crisis'' Trilogy, Lumpawarrump is referred to as Lumpawaroo before undergoing his hrrtayyk ceremony and earning his new name.<ref name="Before the Storm" /> ''A Forest Apart'' asserts that he is eleven years old in 8 ABY,<ref name="A Forest Apart" /> which is only ten years after his birth.<ref name="Rebel Dawn" /><ref name="A Forest Apart" /> [[Leland Chee]], the Keeper of the [[Holocron continuity database]], has confirmed that this is a mistake.<ref name="Leland" /> Although Lumpawaroo's fur is described or depicted as brown or golden-brown in [[Color/Legends|color]] in the majority of his appearances,<ref name="Holiday Special" /><ref name="Fury" /><ref name="The Wookiee Storybook" /> ''Inferno'' describes it as bronze.<ref name="Inferno" /> In the [[1998]] novel ''[[Vision of the Future]]'', Han Solo makes a reference to "Chewbacca's cubs."<ref name="Vision of the Future" /> Although [[The Essential Guide to Alien Species (real-world book)|''The Essential Guide to Alien Species'']] states that Wookiees traditionally bear two to three children, no other canonical source has ever indicated that Lumpawaroo has any siblings.<ref name="EGTAS">[[The Essential Guide to Alien Species (real-world book)|''The Essential Guide to Alien Species'']]</ref> However, a non-canon picture drawn by [[Maya Gohill]] in the 2010 art book [[Star Wars Art: Visions|''Star Wars: Visions'']] depicts Chewbacca and a wife living in a home with three children.<ref name="Visions">''[[Star Wars Art: Visions]]''</ref>
